args.brief: Chapter 3 "The Duplicate". Quiet, practical, third-person past, centred on Pema, so practical actions are precise and nothing is done to the intact wax packet. Foreground the author's intent: Pema has been carrying the dispute's checking work alone out of habit, and in this chapter she learns to accept practical help. Concretely — she reads the handling note that came with the packet and finds a line requiring two people to witness any page comparison; Eli, keeper of the public records, is asked about the missing second page of the tide register, and Pema asks him to fetch the duplicate rather than going herself; Eli brings the duplicate page and Cal sets up a second reading station beside her instead of Pema doing both jobs. Let Pema notice the pull of habit (wanting to do it all herself) and deliberately hand off tasks: Cal reads figures aloud while she writes, Eli signs the handling note as witness. End with the three agreeing, in plain words, that the comparison continues before the public demonstration, with the duplicate page left in its folder for the next session. No injuries; the wax packet stays intact and unopened.
